BiblicalUsage: Tachkemoni was the name carried by Josheb-basshebeth, the Tachmonite, chief of David's mighty men, who lifted his spear against eight hundred and slew them at one time. The Chronicler calls the same man Jashobeam. He is named once under this spelling, at the head of the list of the mighty.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the chief of the mighty earns his place: one man, one spear, eight hundred, and a king who knew the names of the men who fought for him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
